mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) at or below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 5.0 percentage points indicates labor market deterioration that triggers risk-off sentiment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in manufacturing output (INDPRO) and labor force participation (PAYEMS) signals economic contraction that increases equity risk, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in INDPRO and PAYEMS does not produce negative returns in > 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling window, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a rising consumer spending index (RSAFS) relative to housing market activity (HOUST) indicates strong demand that fuels equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansions when RSAFS/HOUST ratio rises, or the signal's Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index 2017=100) indicates manufacturing slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 does not correlate with negative 5-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPIAUCSL change exceeding 3.0 percentage points signals accelerating inflation that prompts monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL yoy change > 3.0 does not produce negative 20-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) above 2.0% indicates robust economic expansion that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 > 2.0% does not correlate with positive 20-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Employment levels (PAYEMS) below 140,000 thousand signal labor market contraction that reduces consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS < 140000 does not produce negative 5-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
